questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why most children want to be astronauts or firefighters
How to make a lot of money from a hotel and a café
Why nurses write books about their patients' lives
Two people who followed their dreams of a better life
questions.why: Beth says they will hear how Daisy and Herman followed their childhood dreams by changing themselves.

questions.q: What did Neil and Beth want to be when they were children?
options: Neil wanted to be an astronaut; Beth a firefighter
Neil a firefighter; Beth an astronaut
They both wanted to travel around the world
They both wanted to be nurses in a hospital
questions.why: Neil wanted to be a fireman, and Beth wanted to be an astronaut and fly to the Moon.

questions.q: How does the Riverside community in New Zealand work?
options: Members' earnings are shared equally between everyone
Members keep the money they earn from their own jobs
Only the people who work the most hours get paid
Members work outside and give half their pay to the group
questions.why: Beth says all the money they earn is collected and shared between everyone equally.

questions.q: According to Daisy, what do many people outside Riverside find hard to accept?
options: That members have to work on the farm every day
That the community doesn't allow any visitors
Everyone gets the same, whatever work they do
That members aren't allowed to leave New Zealand
questions.why: Daisy says no matter how many hours or what work you do, everyone gets the same, and outsiders struggle with this.

questions.q: What does Beth say about the politics of Riverside?
options: Everyone there is a member of the communist party
Members are not allowed to talk about politics
It was started by politicians from East Germany
People with many different views live there
questions.why: Beth says Riverside isn't communist; people with many different political views live there.

questions.q: How did Herman and Candelaria Zapp begin their journey?
options: In an old car with under $3,500
On a plane with their three young children
On bicycles, with money from their families
On a ship, after selling their house in Argentina
questions.why: In 2000 they bought a vintage car and left Argentina with less than 3,500 dollars.

questions.q: How does Herman say travelling has changed him?
options: He now wants to conquer and control the world
He has become more humble by meeting people
He feels tired and wants to go back home
He has become much richer and more successful
questions.why: He says the more people you meet and stories you know, the more humble you become.

questions.q: What does Herman mean when he compares himself to a piece of sand?
options: That he feels lost and alone in the world
That he has spent a lot of time on beaches
Everyone is small but still important
That his journey has been hard and painful
questions.why: He says you are a tiny piece of sand, 'but a very important piece of sand like everyone is'.
